dossier.purpose: SocratiCode is a Node/TypeScript MCP server (npm package `socraticode`, stdio transport only) that indexes a project directory into Qdrant and answers natural-language code queries with `codebase_search`. Each chunk gets a dense embedding plus a server-side BM25 sparse vector, and queries fuse both with RRF. Embeddings come from a configurable provider: Ollama by default (native, managed Docker container or remote), OpenAI, Google Gemini, LM Studio or any OpenAI-compatible /v1/embeddings server, or a LiteLLM proxy. All durable state (chunks, per-file content hashes, indexing status, effective embedding profile, graphs) lives in Qdrant; managed mode runs Qdrant (and optionally Ollama) as Docker containers. The engine exposes 26 MCP tools in total: index lifecycle (index, update, stop, remove, prune, watch), search/status/health, file- and symbol-level dependency/impact graphs, and a separate index of non-code 'context artifacts'. Plugins and extensions for Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, VS Code and Gemini CLI all launch the same `npx -y --prefer-online socraticode@latest` server. The code is dual-licensed AGPL-3.0-only / commercial.

claims.claim: 'Your AI reads code. SocratiCode understands it.' - the open-source codebase context engine: automated knowledge of an entire codebase, zero configuration, fully private, free.

Provides hybrid search, cross-project search, polyglot dependency graphs, symbol-level impact analysis, an interactive graph explorer and searchable context artifacts; zero configuration via any MCP host that supports local stdio servers, or a supported plugin or extension.

Batched, automatic resumable indexing checkpoints progress - pauses, crashes, restarts and interruptions do not lose work; a file watcher keeps the index updated across sessions; multi-branch, multi-repo and multi-agent, with multiple agents sharing a single index.
Production-ready, battle-tested on enterprise-level repositories 'up to and over ~40 million lines of code' (no data or method given).
Private and local by default: Docker handles everything, no API keys required, no data leaves your machine; cloud embeddings (OpenAI, Gemini) and Qdrant Cloud are optional.
Requirements: Node.js >= 18.17 with `npx` on PATH, plus Docker running for the default local Qdrant and Ollama stack.

First use pulls Docker images, starts managed Qdrant and Ollama (or reuses native Ollama in OLLAMA_MODE=auto), downloads the embedding model; ~5 minutes initial setup. First-time indexing: 'under 10 minutes to first-index +3 million lines of code on a Macbook Pro M4'.

By default, server startup resumes the indexed project of the MCP process's working directory: a complete index gets a watcher and an incremental catch-up; an interrupted index resumes from the last checkpoint.
Hybrid code search on Qdrant: each chunk stores a dense vector and a BM25 sparse vector; the Query API runs both sub-queries in one round-trip and fuses them with Reciprocal Rank Fusion.

Multi-provider embeddings - local Ollama, Docker Ollama, OpenAI, Google Gemini, LM Studio (OpenAI-compatible), LiteLLM proxy - switched with a single environment variable; the lmstudio provider also drives other OpenAI-embeddings servers such as HuggingFace TEI.

Incremental indexing with content hashes persisted in Qdrant so state survives restarts; files processed in batches of 50 with progress checkpointed to Qdrant after each batch; already-indexed files are skipped by hash on resume.

Multi-project: each project gets an isolated collection; cross-project search via .socraticode.json linkedProjects or SOCRATICODE_LINKED_PROJECTS with includeLinked:true (each project must be indexed separately); optional branch-aware indexing; committed projectId for team-shared indexes.

Existing collections keep their stored provider/model/dimensions/prefixes; changed settings are reported as pending by codebase_status and are not applied until the collection is removed and re-indexed.
Benchmarked on VS Code (2.45M lines) with Claude Opus 4.6: 61% less context, 84% fewer tool calls, 37x faster than grep-based exploration.

readme.telemetry_and_network: No telemetry, analytics, crash-reporting or self-update-check code in src/ (grep for telemetry|analytics|posthog|sentry|update-check|npm view found nothing); extension/README.md:180 states 'No telemetry from the extension'. No account is needed for the default stack; API keys are only for the optional OpenAI/Google/LiteLLM/Qdrant Cloud paths (README.md:1541-1546, 1573). Network/services touched: (1) Qdrant over HTTP(S) - managed Docker container on localhost:16333 (src/services/docker.ts:121-129; src/constants.ts:43-55) or external QDRANT_URL; an API key is refused over non-HTTPS unless the host is loopback (docker.ts:204-228). It stores chunk text, paths, hashes and graphs. (2) Embedding provider - default Ollama: probes http://localhost:11434/api/tags (src/services/provider-ollama.ts:186), otherwise a Docker container on localhost:11435, and pulls the nomic-embed-text model on first use (provider-ollama.ts:264-268); optional OpenAI API (provider-openai.ts:53), Google Generative AI API (provider-google.ts:65), LM Studio/any OpenAI-compatible server (provider-lmstudio.ts:63), LiteLLM proxy (provider-litellm.ts:92). With cloud providers, chunk text prefixed with the file path is sent off-machine (SECURITY.md:31-33; src/services/embeddings.ts:148-158). (3) Docker Hub pulls of qdrant/qdrant:v1.17.0 and ollama/ollama:latest (constants.ts:55,99; docker.ts:63-79,267-283). (4) npm registry: the documented launcher `npx -y --prefer-online socraticode@latest` checks npm on every server start (README.md:109,123; .claude-plugin/mcp.json:8). (5) codebase_graph_visualize writes an HTML file to the OS temp dir and opens the default browser; Cytoscape/Dagre are vendored, no CDN (src/services/graph-visualize-browser.ts:23-46; README.md:1258). Logs go to MCP notifications/stderr or an optional local SOCRATICODE_LOG_FILE (src/services/logger.ts:9-12,33-42). The server listens on no port (stdio only: src/index.ts:467-468; SECURITY.md:27; no http server code in src/). 'SocratiCode Cloud' is a separate hosted product (README.md:42, 1865-1880); src/ contains no reference to it.

code.architecture: MCP stdio server. src/index.ts registers 26 tools and delegates to src/tools/{index,query,graph,context,manage}-tools.ts, which call src/services/*. Identity/scoping (src/config.ts): project id = first 12 hex chars of sha256(path.resolve(projectPath)) (config.ts:194-197), overridable by SOCRATICODE_PROJECT_ID or .socraticode.json projectId, optional git-branch suffix; collections codebase_<id>, codegraph_<id>, context_<id> (config.ts:221-239), optional QDRANT_COLLECTION_PREFIX; linkedProjects for cross-project search. Infra: services/docker.ts (docker CLI wrapper running managed qdrant/qdrant:v1.17.0 and ollama/ollama:latest containers; external-Qdrant health check with API-key/TLS guard). Storage/search: services/qdrant.ts (collections with Cosine dense + idf-BM25 sparse vectors, batched upserts with retry, hybrid prefetch+RRF query, multi-collection merge by cosine, and a `socraticode_metadata` collection holding per-project file-hash map, indexing status, effective profile and graph pointers; qdrant.ts:1336-1500). Indexing: services/indexer.ts (discovery with built-in ignores + .gitignore + .socraticodeignore via services/ignore.ts; 5 MB file cap; files <=100 lines become one chunk, larger ones are ast-grep AST-chunked with 100-line/10-overlap line fallback, character chunking for minified files, 2000-char cap; 50-file embed->upsert->checkpoint batches with cancellation; indexer.ts:740-822,1287-1399), services/index-profile.ts (per-collection effective profile pinning provider/model/dimensions/prefixes/chunk format). Embeddings: services/embeddings.ts (batch 32, 3 retries), embedding-provider.ts, provider-{ollama,openai,google,lmstudio,litellm}.ts, embedding-config.ts. Lifecycle: startup.ts (auto-resume, graceful shutdown), watcher.ts (@parcel/watcher, 2 s debounce), git-refresh.ts/git-state.ts (SOCRATICODE_WATCHER=git), lock.ts (proper-lockfile under os.tmpdir()/socraticode-locks, 2 min stale), reclamation-barrier.ts (codebase_prune). Graphs: code-graph.ts, graph-*.ts and symbol-graph-*.ts (static analysis persisted in Qdrant), graph-visualize-*.ts + src/assets (vendored Cytoscape/Dagre HTML). context-artifacts.ts indexes non-code documents listed in .socraticodecontextartifacts.json. Search returns top-N chunks (default 10, max 50) above minScore 0.10 (constants.ts:105-114).
code.packaging_and_release: Artifacts: (a) npm package `socraticode` (package.json:2-4; `files` whitelist :53-65 = dist, .claude-plugin, skills, agents, hooks, .mcp.json, licenses, README; built by `tsc && node scripts/copy-assets.mjs` on prepublishOnly :12,19; dist/ is git-ignored, .gitignore:2). (b) VS Code extension .vsix published to the VS Code Marketplace and Open VSX and attached to the GitHub Release (.github/workflows/extension-release.yml:48-63, triggered by tags v* or manual). (c) MCP Registry entry server.json, published by .github/workflows/mcp-registry-release.yml on tags v*: verifies tag/manifest versions, waits until the exact npm version exists, installs mcp-publisher 1.8.1 after a sha256 check, authenticates with GitHub OIDC (id-token: write), publishes (mcp-registry-release.yml:10,29-90). (d) Plugin manifests (.claude-plugin, .codex-plugin, .cursor-plugin, gemini-extension.json) are distributed by git tag/clone (README.md:352-367). npm publish, git tag and GitHub Release are produced by a maintainer running `release-it` (.release-it.json:1-18; DEVELOPER.md:158-174); no file in .github/workflows publishes to npm. No checksums, signatures, SLSA/npm provenance or attestations for the npm tarball or .vsix were found (grep for provenance|attest|sigstore|cosign|slsa|checksum|gpg over workflows, package.json, scripts and release config returned only the mcp-publisher sha256 pin, mcp-registry-release.yml:70,79). Actions are tag-pinned (@v7) in ci.yml/extension-*.yml but SHA-pinned in mcp-registry-release.yml:22,24. Manifest version coupling is enforced by scripts/check-release-versions.mjs (run in ci.yml:23). Cadence: 49 changelog entries, 1.0.1 (2026-03-04) to 1.16.0 (2026-09-28) (CHANGELOG.md:7,827). The v1.16.0 tag is annotated and peels to the commit above (.git/packed-refs:2-3).

Not run in CI: tests/e2e and 11 of the 18 integration files; no macOS runner; no coverage threshold (vitest.config.ts:21-26).
code.dependencies: Root package.json: 34 runtime dependencies (@ast-grep/napi plus 16 @ast-grep/lang-* grammars, @modelcontextprotocol/sdk, @qdrant/js-client-rest ~1.18, ollama, openai, @google/generative-ai, @parcel/watcher, proper-lockfile, glob, ignore, undici ^6, web-tree-sitter, @lumis-sh/wasm-eex/heex, smol-toml, open, zod, @hono/node-server), 1 optionalDependency (tree-sitter-gdscript 6.1.0) and 9 devDependencies, plus npm `overrides` for vite/postcss/undici (package.json:66-127); package-lock.json present. @hono/node-server is declared (package.json:85) but nothing in src/ imports it (grep). extension/package.json: 0 runtime dependencies and 8 devDependencies (extension/package.json:212-221); extension/package-lock.json present. Non-npm runtime requirements: Docker CLI (managed mode), Qdrant >= 1.15.2 (managed image v1.17.0), an embedding service (Ollama by default), optional git (branch-aware and git-refresh modes). THIRD-PARTY-LICENSES lists the runtime/dev dependencies as MIT, Apache-2.0, ISC or BSD-3-Clause.
code.security_policy: SECURITY.md (root): report privately by email to giancarlo@altaire.com, not via public issues; acknowledgement within 48 hours and a detailed response within 7 days; only the latest release is supported; a GitHub security advisory is published after the fix; scope is the SocratiCode codebase and its managed Docker containers, not third-party services (SECURITY.md:3-48). No GitHub private-vulnerability-reporting configuration is present in .github/.

claim_checks.claim: Hybrid search: dense vector + BM25 sparse vector fused with RRF in one Qdrant Query API call (README.md:560).
claim_checks.evidence: src/services/qdrant.ts:955-976 builds one `query` with two prefetch legs (dense `using:'dense'` and bm25 `{text, model:'qdrant/bm25'}`) and `query:{fusion:'rrf'}`; collections are created with a Cosine dense vector and an idf-modified sparse `bm25` vector (qdrant.ts:144-160). BM25 inference is server-side and needs Qdrant >= 1.15.2 (comment at qdrant.ts:873; README.md:1611); there is no runtime server-version check (client built with checkCompatibility:false, qdrant.ts:119,125).

claim_checks.claim: Batched, resumable indexing: 50-file batches checkpointed to Qdrant; interruptions do not lose work; content hashes persisted in Qdrant so state survives restarts (README.md:568-569, 1709-1714).
claim_checks.evidence: INDEX_BATCH_SIZE=50 (src/constants.ts:120). Each batch embeds, upserts, then writes the hash map plus status 'in-progress' to a point in the `socraticode_metadata` collection (src/services/indexer.ts:1287-1399; qdrant.ts:1336,1462-1500). Unchanged files are skipped by content hash (indexer.ts:1226). A partial upsert throws before hashes advance (qdrant.ts:844-854; indexer.ts:1367-1379). Resume from 'in-progress' first reconciles hashes with stored points (indexer.ts:1115-1128) and is covered by tests/integration/interrupted-resume-recovery.test.ts, which CI runs against a real Qdrant with stubbed embeddings (ci.yml:183-187). Granularity is one batch, and the whole hash map is rewritten at each checkpoint (qdrant.ts:1475-1496).

claim_checks.claim: Private and local by default; no API keys; no data leaves the machine; the default Docker setup makes no external API calls (README.md:48, 564; SECURITY.md:26).
claim_checks.evidence: Defaults are provider=ollama, OLLAMA_MODE=auto, QDRANT_MODE=managed (src/services/embedding-config.ts:271,339; src/constants.ts:52-53) and the only probe is to localhost (provider-ollama.ts:186), so code content stays local in default mode. First use still needs network: docker pull of qdrant/qdrant:v1.17.0 and ollama/ollama:latest (docker.ts:63-79,267-283), an Ollama model pull (provider-ollama.ts:264-268) and an npm lookup at every launch with @latest (README.md:109). docs/guides/local-only.md:16 acknowledges the downloads; SECURITY.md:26's 'No external API calls are made' is narrower in practice than worded.

claim_checks.claim: Multi-provider embeddings (Ollama, Docker Ollama, OpenAI, Gemini, LM Studio/OpenAI-compatible, LiteLLM) 'with a single environment variable' (README.md:563, 934-936).
claim_checks.evidence: Five providers are implemented and chosen by EMBEDDING_PROVIDER (src/services/embedding-provider.ts:48-79; embedding-config.ts:271-283). The 'lmstudio' provider uses the OpenAI SDK against any /v1/embeddings server with encoding_format 'float' (provider-lmstudio.ts:3-24,327-331) and an opt-in /v1/embeddings probe when /v1/models is missing (TEI). It is not a single variable: lmstudio and litellm refuse to start without EMBEDDING_MODEL and EMBEDDING_DIMENSIONS (litellm also LITELLM_API_KEY), and openai/google need API keys (embedding-config.ts:288-336; provider-openai.ts:46-52). The README itself states these extras at README.md:925-927, 988-991.

claim_checks.claim: Existing collections keep their stored provider/model/dimensions/prefixes; requested changes are reported as pending and never auto-applied; remove + re-index to activate (README.md:1517, 1598).
claim_checks.evidence: resolveEffectiveIndexProfile returns the stored profile when one exists (src/services/index-profile.ts:155-172); search, update and indexing run inside withEffectiveEmbedding(profile) (index-profile.ts:180-194; qdrant.ts:911-921; indexer.ts:1342); codebase_status lists pending differences (src/tools/query-tools.ts:292-315). Caveat: only vector-defining values are overridden - URLs and credentials still come from the live process env (embedding-config.ts:462-466).

claim_checks.claim: Multiple agents share one index; cross-process file locks (proper-lockfile) with stale-lock reclaim after 2 minutes; one watcher per project (README.md:585-586, 1818-1824).
claim_checks.evidence: Locks are files in os.tmpdir()/socraticode-locks with stale=120 s (src/services/lock.ts:27-33), taken non-reentrantly by indexProject (indexer.ts:1056-1067) and startWatching (watcher.ts:261-266). The README itself limits this to one host with the same temp directory (README.md:1812-1814, 1197). Each process caches the file-hash map after first load (indexer.ts:253-274) and invalidates it only for Git-refresh runs (indexer.ts:1095,1612); watcher/resume settings are per process and must match across processes (README.md:1592; DEVELOPER.md:867).

claim_checks.claim: By default, server startup resumes the indexed project of the MCP process's working directory (README.md:129, 580).
claim_checks.evidence: The resume logic matches (src/services/startup.ts:222-332), but in managed mode it returns early if Docker is unavailable or the Qdrant container is not already running - it does not start them (startup.ts:71-80) - and it skips when cwd is '/' or $HOME (startup.ts:103-107). SOCRATICODE_AUTO_RESUME=off returns before any Docker/Qdrant access (startup.ts:63-67). The README does not mention the not-running or cwd conditions; the code governs.

claim_checks.claim: README env table: OLLAMA_HOST is the 'Ollama base URL (alternative to OLLAMA_URL)' (README.md:1538).
claim_checks.evidence: The Ollama client host comes only from OLLAMA_URL (src/services/embedding-config.ts:384; provider-ollama.ts:60). OLLAMA_HOST is read only at src/constants.ts:97 and used only for the Docker container readiness poll (docker.ts:318,341), so setting it alone does not redirect embedding calls. Code differs from README.

claim_checks.claim: Docker isolation: Qdrant and Ollama containers expose only the necessary ports on localhost (SECURITY.md:28).
claim_checks.evidence: src/services/docker.ts:121-129 and 325-332 publish `-p <port>:<container-port>` with no host address (docker-compose.yml:6-8,16-17 likewise) and configure no Qdrant API key. benchmarks.what: VS Code repo (~2.45M lines, 5,300+ files, 55,437 chunks), 5 architectural questions, Claude Opus 4.6: context bytes consumed by a scripted grep-style multi-step exploration vs one codebase_search call returning 10 chunks. risks: Update path and supply chain: every documented launcher runs `npx -y --prefer-online socraticode@latest`, so each MCP server start resolves and executes whatever npm tags `latest` (.mcp.json:4-6; .claude-plugin/mcp.json:5-9; README.md:109,195). Pinning via SOCRATICODE_SPEC exists for the Claude Code plugin only; Codex and Cursor read the fixed .mcp.json (README.md:211). Releases are published from a maintainer machine with release-it (.release-it.json:16-18; DEVELOPER.md:158-174); no workflow publishes to npm and no provenance, signature or checksum for the npm tarball or .vsix was found. The `ollama/ollama:latest` image is unpinned (src/constants.ts:99; docker-compose.yml:14; ci.yml:62) while Qdrant is pinned to v1.17.0 (constants.ts:55).

Container exposure: managed Qdrant and Ollama are started with `-p 16333:6333`, `-p 16334:6334`, `-p 11435:11434`, no host address and no Qdrant API key or auth (src/services/docker.ts:121-129, 325-332; docker-compose.yml:6-8,16-17). Docker publishes unqualified ports on all host interfaces unless the daemon is configured otherwise, whereas SECURITY.md:28 says 'exposed on localhost'. Qdrant payloads hold full chunk text (src/services/qdrant.ts:735-744; indexer.ts:1355-1364).

Data exposure: no secret detection or redaction exists in src/ (grep). The default index covers json/yaml/toml/ini/cfg/txt/md/sql (src/constants.ts:335-340) and `.env.example` (constants.ts:395); dot-directories are excluded unless INCLUDE_DOT_FILES=true (README.md:1581). Chunk text prefixed with the file path goes to the configured embedding endpoint (src/services/embeddings.ts:148-158) and leaves the machine with openai/google/litellm (SECURITY.md:31-33). Search results return raw chunk content to the host assistant (src/tools/query-tools.ts:204-209), which has its own provider boundary (docs/guides/local-only.md:16).

Two-client operation (Claude Code + Codex): each client starts its own engine process. Locks are files under os.tmpdir()/socraticode-locks (src/services/lock.ts:27), so they only coordinate processes on one host with the same temp dir (README.md:1812-1814, 1197). The per-process file-hash cache is loaded once and invalidated only for Git-refresh runs (indexer.ts:253-274, 1095, 1612). Watcher/resume modes are per-process settings that must match (README.md:1592; DEVELOPER.md:867). Index identity is sha256 of the absolute path (src/config.ts:194-197) unless a projectId is pinned. The Codex plugin has no documented per-user env override for its bundled server (README.md:248) and plugin-bundled servers may not inherit a direct server's env (README.md:1438); a collection's stored profile fixes provider/model/dimensions but credentials and URLs are read from each process's own env (src/services/embedding-config.ts:462-466).

State and scale: all durable state is in Qdrant; there is no export, backup or snapshot tooling in src/ (grep). The whole file-hash map is serialised as one JSON string in one metadata point and re-upserted after every 50-file batch (src/services/qdrant.ts:1475-1496; indexer.ts:1389-1397), unlike the sharded symbol graph (constants.ts:249-253); Qdrant's default request limit is 32 MiB (constants.ts:142-147). Managed data sits in the Docker volume `socraticode_qdrant_data` (docker.ts:126) and removing it discards the index (DEVELOPER.md:1713-1717). Server-side BM25 needs Qdrant >= 1.15.2 on external instances with no runtime version check (README.md:1611; qdrant.ts:119,125,873).

Platform and test coverage: CI uses ubuntu-latest plus one windows-latest job running 3 git unit-test files; there is no macOS or WSL2 runner (.github/workflows/ci.yml:15,29,42-53). tests/e2e and 11 of the 18 integration files do not run in CI (ci.yml:55-237). The managed Docker Ollama container has no GPU options (src/services/docker.ts:325-332), so GPU use needs native/external Ollama or a hosted provider (README.md:609-613). Default managed mode needs the `docker` CLI and a running daemon (docker.ts:41-48; README.md:83), and OLLAMA_MODE=auto falls back to Docker when nothing answers on localhost:11434 (provider-ollama.ts:198-202).

Maintenance and licensing: single copyright holder and listed author (Giancarlo Erra - Altaire Limited; package.json:39-43; README.md:1896); 49 changelog releases between 2026-03-04 and 2026-09-28 (CHANGELOG.md:7,827); only the latest release receives security fixes (SECURITY.md:35-42). Dual-licensed AGPL-3.0-only / commercial (LICENSE; LICENSE-COMMERCIAL:1-15) with a CLA granting the owner rights to relicense contributions (CLA.md:21-27); a hosted 'SocratiCode Cloud' is in private beta (README.md:42, 1865-1880). The vendored Cytoscape.js/Dagre bundles in src/assets, shipped in dist/assets via scripts/copy-assets.mjs:14-19, are not listed in THIRD-PARTY-LICENSES (:6-43).

Docs-vs-code and scoping behaviours: README.md:1538 presents OLLAMA_HOST as an alternative to OLLAMA_URL, but the client reads only OLLAMA_URL (src/services/embedding-config.ts:384; docker.ts:318,341). Startup auto-resume does nothing when Docker/Qdrant are not already running or cwd is '/' or $HOME (startup.ts:71-80,103-107). Context-artifact config silently falls back to ~/.claude/arch/.socraticodecontextartifacts.json or SOCRATICODE_GLOBAL_CONFIG_DIR, which README/DEVELOPER do not document (src/services/context-artifacts.ts:87-91). Scope is the `projectPath` argument or the server's cwd (src/tools/query-tools.ts:126,135), `fileFilter` is an exact relative-path match only (src/services/qdrant.ts:944-946), and a linked project whose query fails is dropped with only a log warning (qdrant.ts:1170-1176).
